Autopsy validation shows late-stage flortaucipir uptake differs across primary cortex

Among 155 autopsy-confirmed Alzheimer cases, flortaucipir uptake in primary isocortices began at Braak stage V, with visual and auditory regions increasing earlier and faster than motor and somatosensory regions.

Important new evidence•Peer-reviewed autopsy-confirmed PET-pathology study•September 23, 2026

Autopsy validation shows late-stage flortaucipir uptake differs across primary cortex

Among 155 autopsy-confirmed Alzheimer cases, flortaucipir uptake in primary isocortices began at Braak stage V, with visual and auditory regions increasing earlier and faster than motor and somatosensory regions.

Key quantitative results: The analysis included 155 autopsy-confirmed participants with Alzheimer disease.

BiomarkersTau PETFlortaucipir tau PETBraak neurofibrillary tangle stageBiological staging

Added October 16, 2026 · DOI:10.1016/j.isci.2026.117530; PMID:42830961; PMCID:PMC13634365

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

Primary isocortex is usually emphasized as the terminal Braak stage, but uptake was not uniform. Visual and auditory cortex showed earlier and steeper flortaucipir increases than motor and somatosensory cortex, and age and APOE ε4 influenced uptake. The result refines late-stage spatial interpretation without validating a new treatment-selection threshold.

Study design

Researchers measured flortaucipir uptake in primary visual, auditory, motor and somatosensory isocortices in 155 participants with autopsy-confirmed Alzheimer disease, then related regional uptake to neuropathologic Braak stage and clinical or genetic covariates.

Key quantitative results

  • The analysis included 155 autopsy-confirmed participants with Alzheimer disease.
  • Flortaucipir uptake in primary isocortices became apparent beginning at Braak stage V.
  • Visual and auditory isocortices showed greater and faster uptake increases than somatosensory and motor cortex.
  • Age and APOE ε4 influenced uptake; primary-isocortex patterns resembled lateral temporal cortex more than entorhinal cortex.

What changed

The pathology-anchored analysis shows that primary cortical regions do not behave as one homogeneous late-stage tau-PET compartment and that visual/auditory regions may signal advanced spread earlier than traditionally emphasized.

Strength of evidence

Moderate-to-strong clinical-validity evidence because diagnosis and Braak stage were autopsy confirmed and the cohort was sizeable for pathology studies. The analysis remains cross-sectional and tracer-specific, and clinical utility was not tested.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Regional late-stage flortaucipir interpretation may need to distinguish visual and auditory cortex from motor and somatosensory cortex. The findings do not create a new authorized stage, threshold or treatment-eligibility rule.

Field medical relevance

Relevant to tau-PET visual and quantitative staging, spatial reporting, pathology concordance and discussions of how late-stage regional uptake should be interpreted.

Quanterix or platform relevance

The study links regional flortaucipir uptake to neuropathologically confirmed Braak stage. It supports regional interpretation for this tracer but does not establish equivalence with other tau tracers, visual-staging schemes or quantitative pipelines.

Access or reimbursement relevance

No new availability or coverage change. The study may inform specialist interpretation but does not expand access to tau PET.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Does uptake in primary cortex define a new clinical stage?
No. The study refines regional relationships with neuropathologic Braak stage but does not validate a new clinical staging system.
Can the pattern be generalized to every tau tracer?
No. The evidence is specific to flortaucipir and requires tracer-specific replication.
Was treatment eligibility or response tested?
No. This was a PET-pathology interpretation study.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Historical criteria-repair backfill rather than a newly published item
  • Cross-sectional analysis
  • Tracer-specific findings
  • Potential interval between PET and autopsy
  • No prospective visual-reading or treatment-decision utility test
